title: I've got the signal!
author: rutan668
selftext: I was about to give up and then Astra came along with a whole new method and now I've got a profitable signal. Problem is that now other people can get it too which likely makes it useless, so the real question and issue is the AI arms race and whether there will even be time to implement it and take the profits that it promises.  AI companies have their own even more powerful AI's so who knows what they are doing in house?  Maybe I'll just have something for weeks or months and then it will all be over.  If I alone had the technology then that would be one thing but anyone can access the same tech and that's what makes this situation more fraught than just signal or no signal.  Where are other people at with this?

comments.author: EmergencyFly6361
comments.body: This is what Elon Musk meant by ‘singularity’ that we’ll reach due to advances in AI. It’s an abstract concept for now which seems plausible but hard to define what it exactly is going to be like.

comments.author: Bergodrake
comments.body:
I think the key distinction is between using an LLM to find a signal and actually building an ML system around it. LLMs can come up with interesting strategies, but the hard part is proving they work out-of-sample, avoiding overfitting, handling regime changes, and continuously testing thousands of variations against historical data.

I actually built Trigol (my AI stock prediction engine) around this idea. 

 Access to the same LLM isn’t the same thing as having the same data, pipeline, models, validation process and research behind it. That's where the real edge is.
